title: Naturality and identity-composition square of the finite partial tensor comparison
statement: Fix a finite six-functor operation datum S [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and a finite-type space X. Let A be its full bounded constructible finite coefficient category and B the finite-Tor bounded constructible category. Let U be identity pullback on A, V its restriction to B, and T:A×B→A the uncurried partial tensor of [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates]. Let c_M:U(M)≅U(U(M)) be the supplied pullback compositor for identity followed by identity, precomposed with the equality transport from identity to its square; define d_L:V(L)≅V(V(L)) by the same construction through the full finite-Tor inclusion. The components of [def-sf-finite-partial-pullback-tensor] form a natural isomorphism μ:T⋙U≅(U×V)⋙T, and satisfy μ_{M,L} followed by T(c_M,d_L) = c_{T(M,L)} followed by U(μ_{M,L}) followed by μ_{U(M),V(L)}, for every M in A and L in B. No identity unit is among the data or the conclusion.

proof.text: The fixed prime-to-characteristic setting makes the coefficient prime invertible on X. Write n=m+1 using hn. Apply the faithful full bounded-constructible inclusion and undo the coefficient realization. The comparison becomes canonical fixed-scalar tensor/pullback conjugated by the specified pullRealization, fixedPullRealization and equivalence units. Naturality of these maps yields a natural isomorphism on the partial domains, with exactly the prescribed components.

Expand both composite routes under that inclusion. Move coefficient-equivalence units using naturality and cancel adjacent inverse pairs. The remaining square is the canonical finite tensor/pullback composition equation. finitePullCompositionNormalization identifies the supplied compositor with this canonical one; its full finite-Tor restriction identifies the second-variable compositor. Transport identity squared to identity and reflect the resulting equality through the faithful inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem finitePartialTensor_identityComposition
    (S : SixFunctorFiniteOperations D C E n hn) (X : SixFunctorSpace D) :
    let U := S.finite.pull (𝟙 X)
    let V := CompactSupportFiniteProjection.torPull S (𝟙 X)
    let T := Functor.uncurry.obj (CompactSupportFiniteProjection.partialTensor S X)
    let c : ∀ M, U.obj M ≅ U.obj (U.obj M) := fun M ↦
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ (S.finite.pull f).obj M)
        (Category.id_comp (𝟙 X)).symm) ≪≫
        (S.finite.pullComposition (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)).app M
    let d : ∀ L, V.obj L ≅ V.obj (V.obj L) := fun L ↦
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ (CompactSupportFiniteProjection.torPull S f).obj L)
        (Category.id_comp (𝟙 X)).symm) ≪≫
        CompactSupportFiniteProjection.torPullComposition S (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X) L
    ∃ μ : T ⋙ U ≅ U.prod V ⋙ T,
      (∀ M L, μ.app (M, L) =
        CompactSupportFiniteProjection.pullbackTensorComparison S (𝟙 X) M L) ∧
      (∀ M L, μ.hom.app (M, L) ≫
          T.map (Prod.mkHom (c M).hom (d L).hom) =
        (c (T.obj (M, L))).hom ≫ U.map (μ.hom.app (M, L)) ≫
          μ.hom.app (U.obj M, V.obj L))
